runs.text: I arrived with a past that spoke too loudly.
They did not sell miracles. They handed me a plan.
Calendar blocks that respected a life already on fire.
Hope came back in measurable units.
One finished project. One mock interview.
instead of fear I could not.
Errors turned into lessons with names.
I learned to trust what I build.
Skills stacked like bricks, not wishes.
Numbers moved in the right direction.
The past became context, not a verdict.
A data point, not a destiny.
I can learn, I can elevate, I can lead.
Merit America did not rewrite me.
It let me write the next chapter.
He did not hand me fixes.
He made the room better by raising the floor, not lowering the bar.
When I reached for excuses, he reached for questions.
“How could you have done that better?”
“What could you have done differently, Amy?”
If I tried to host a pity party, he turned off the music.
Ball back in my court. Play the point.
He walked beside me, never ahead with answers, never behind with blame.
Progress over comfort. Clarity over consolation.
I learned to review my own tape, to name the miss, to plan the next rep.
Not by carrying me, but by making me strong enough to carry it myself.
what had already spilled out on the floor.
You want to know what changed?
That I had to be ready,
He broke the door off the fucking hinges
He showed up in jail cells,
bathroom mirrors I couldn’t look into
He showed up when I told Him not to.
isn’t with a robe and trumpet
This is the God who waits in parking lots.
Who sits with you in the void
while your heart bleeds out quietly
in meetings you need to be at.
Because the miracle isn’t the timing.

Forward two from my starting position, I lean into the game, detached from any preconceived outcome. My bishop takes his knight in a swift left-swipe action. A bold move in this world of strategy and surprise.
In my mind, I list all possible moves, plotting each square, calculating each consequence. He moves two squares, his lowered eyes giving nothing away. A dance of intentions, a game of wits.
My rook is eager, waiting for its move. Both pieces have yet to dance, with no barriers between. A thick tension fills the space we share, each of us anticipating the unfolding play.
Black to move, the board holds its breath.
All my counting, all my planning. Every possibility examined; every risk weighed.
Then out of nowhere he castles by queenside, shifting the balance of my reality.
In this game of chess, in this fleeting encounter, I can see the parallels to our moments together. Every move, every glance, a calculated risk. A strategic dance of hearts and minds.
Checkmate, but not in victory or defeat. Rather, in the realization that our brief time shared a game of life played out on 64 squares, where love and logic intertwine and surprises await.
